correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed directly from the source inverse formulas. Finite alternating-sign inputs of norm one make a chosen output coordinate equal to the positive partial geometric sum, giving lower bounds tending to \(\max\{1,1/(a-1)\}\) for \((\Phi_E^a)^{-1}\) and independently to \(1/(b-1)\) and \(b/[c(b-1)]\) for \((\Psi_E^{b,c})^{-1}\). Since ordinary norm is at most regular norm and the source majorants give the reverse inequalities, both equalities follow. Piecewise monotonicity gives the unique \(a=2\) minimum \(3\), fixed-\(b\) minimizer \(c=b\), and unattained infimum \(1\) as \(b\to\infty\).

value.rationale: These are the exact local quantitative costs of the two elementary maps at the core of a new positive Cantor--Bernstein construction. Sharpness distinguishes which local estimates can or cannot be improved and identifies a genuine barrier \(3\) for one family versus asymptotic distortion \(1\) for the other. The object and invariant are therefore naturally motivated rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, even though the proof is short.
residual_risks: The result does not prove sharpness of the paper's final global Miljutin constant.
